note: Lake Erie story based on NASA MODIS-Aqua chlorophyll-a observations, July–October, 2003–2025. Trends calculated using Mann-Kendall and Sen's slope.

steps.title: The lake we share
steps.text: Lake Erie connects communities across Canada and the United States, including Windsor-Essex. Its waters support drinking water supplies, fishing, recreation, and local ecosystems. Understanding long-term environmental changes helps communities make informed decisions.

steps.title: What the satellites saw
steps.text: We analyzed NASA MODIS-Aqua chlorophyll-a observations from July through October for each year between 2003 and 2025. Across Lake Erie, chlorophyll-a increased by approximately 1.55 mg/m³ per decade. The Mann-Kendall test found this upward trend statistically significant (p < 0.001).

steps.title: Where it's changing
steps.text: Both major regions show significant upward trends. The Western Basin increased by approximately 1.34 mg/m³ per decade, while the Eastern Basin increased by approximately 1.39 mg/m³ per decade. Explore the satellite pixel map to discover where changes are statistically significant and where they are not.

steps.title: Why it matters for Windsor-Essex
steps.text: Chlorophyll-a is an indicator of phytoplankton abundance. Tracking its changes can help researchers understand shifts in lake conditions and identify areas for further investigation. However, rising chlorophyll-a alone does not establish that harmful algal blooms are increasing or that drinking water is unsafe.

steps.title: Explore it yourself
steps.text: Use the Trend Scanner to inspect the NASA chlorophyll-a results. Select Whole Lake, Western Basin, or Eastern Basin to compare historical patterns. Click individual satellite pixels on the map to examine their trend direction, rate of change, and statistical significance.
